Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: production 2D pixel-art animation SPRITE SHEET for the exact baby creature in reference image 1. Reference image 1 is the approved CHARACTER IDENTITY reference, not a sheet to copy. Create ONE transparent PNG sprite sheet, landscape 4:3 aspect ratio, exactly FOUR equally sized columns and THREE equally sized rows, 12 cells total, no gaps between cells and no drawn cell borders. Each cell is one animation frame. All cells have identical invisible canvas bounds, same 96x96 logical pixel scale, consistent palette, line weight, camera angle and baseline. Draw ONE complete creature per cell, including tail, with 10% transparent padding inside every cell so nothing touches a neighbor or cell edge. Keep the exact reference creature's head, facial markings, appendages, proportions and colors across all 12 frames. Keep chunky polished pixel-art aesthetic; simple strong poses readable on a 96px handheld screen. Front or slight three-quarter facing consistent within each row.
Top row, left to right: 4 looping SLEEP frames: this same creature curled low on its belly with chin resting on paws and eyes FULLY CLOSED, gentle breathing cycle exhale/inhale/full inhale/return; ears/wings/horns and tail remain recognizable, tiny movement only, no props or blanket, no text or Z symbols.
Middle row, left to right: 4 looping EAT frames: same creature awake seated, holding one small cream bowl with a few orange food pieces; frame1 holding bowl at belly; frame2 lifting a bite with one paw toward mouth; frame3 eyes contentedly closed while chewing and cheeks puffed, bowl still held; frame4 smiling after swallowing with bowl at belly again. Bowl/paws visibly change pose, body retains size.
Bottom row, left to right: 4 looping PLAY frames: same creature awake playing with one small coral-red ball on the ground; frame1 paw reaching toward ball at its side; frame2 leaning and pushing ball; frame3 excited small hop reaching for ball; frame4 landing and returning paw, ready to repeat frame1. Keep ball inside cell padding. Clearly distinct full poses, no ghost limbs, no duplicate tails.
Constraints: exactly 12 isolated sprites, 4 columns x 3 rows, equal-grid frames, TRUE transparent alpha background, no checkerboard painted into pixels, NO labels/numbers/watermark/frame lines/scenery/shadows. Preserve reference identity; do not invent a different species or add accessories beyond eating bowl and playing ball.
Identity lock: Forest Yaya: mint pear-shaped body, two broad leaf ears, small green sprout on head, two dark green cheek chevrons, cream belly and short curled leaf-ended tail.
